A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RL-D2 study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original DNA-generation, MinAtar, Atari and Google Research Football experiments, including performance, computational costs and appendix ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and reports additional baseline comparisons, budget and hyperparameter studies, and statistical analyses.

M1.justification: Section 4.1 removes the optional ELBO-difference importance-ratio approximation presented in v1, retaining the existing augmented-MDP single-step ratio. The PMD framework, FKL/RKL objective families, on-policy diffusion learning and appendix planner algorithm remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The enhancer-generation task, MinAtar and Atari benchmarks, and eight Football environments are retained. The added '11 vs 11 SM' comparison changes the training budget within an existing task, rather than introducing a new environment or task requirement.

E2.justification: Football Table 2 adds separately evaluated MAT and MAPPO baselines alongside the retained autoregressive comparator, substantially strengthening this comparison. MAT is distinguished by randomized agent ordering, rather than merely renaming the original comparator. The revised planner comparison also adds a standard RL-D2 reference in Figure 14.

E3.justification: Appendix D.4 changes Football training from 100M to 1B steps for 11 vs 11 and from 10M/100M to 500M elsewhere. Table 4 revises learning rates, rollout length, entropy weight and gradient clipping. v3 also adds matched-wall-time FKL/RKL batch-size comparisons, a 100M-step Football control, and Atari median/IQM metrics. The planner evaluation changes its sample range and tested planning lengths.

E4.justification: v3 adds FKL/RKL compute and sample-efficiency comparisons, DQN-Macro hyperparameter searches, and Atari/Football KL-constraint sensitivity studies that expose learning instability and collapse. The existing planner analysis is revised. MinAtar temperature tuning, on-policy diffusion and architecture ablations were already present in v1 and are retained.

E5.justification: MinAtar Table 1 changes the reported seed count from 3 to 20 and introduces bootstrap confidence limits. Football Table 2 newly specifies bootstrap intervals over 20 seeds. Appendix D.5 adds 50,000-iteration stratified bootstrapping for Atari aggregate statistics and performance differences; this does not establish an increased Atari run count.

E6.justification: MinAtar and Football table entries are revised, and numerous comparative and sensitivity results are added. Football's reported 11 vs 11 RKL score changes from 54.2 to 99.4 under revised budgets and hyperparameters, so this is not a same-setting gain. The new small-budget comparison reports FKL 68.5 versus RKL 0.0. The full per-game Atari Table 5 is unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 corrects the PMD normalization in Eq. (3), removes the erroneous leading minus signs from the ELBO expressions in Eqs. (4) and (5), and makes the masking transition consistent with its cumulative schedule. It removes Appendix B.3's ELBO-ratio bias derivation. The principal FKL/RKL proofs and temperature-duality derivation remain.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies superiority over baselines as 'comparable or superior' and adds an explicit FKL sample-efficiency versus RKL stability/asymptotic-performance trade-off. The central PMD-based diffusion-policy contribution, introduction's contribution list and concluding scope remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: New Section 5.4 and expanded Appendix E.3 provide substantive guidance on choosing FKL versus RKL. They explain rapid FKL exploitation, RKL's more gradual clipped updates, and temperature-dependent collapse, proposing loss of replay diversity as a mechanism. v3 also discusses autoregressive ordering mitigation and qualifies scalability comparisons that v1 described more categorically.

D1.justification: v3 documents DQN-Macro search grids, KL-constraint schedules and the trajectory interpretation of Atari batch sizes, and revises Football implementation parameters. Most architecture and DNA-processing details remain unchanged. Conversely, v1's explicit identification of the four Atari scaling-study games is omitted.

R1.justification: Section 2, Remark 1 and Appendix G add focused positioning against evolution strategies, genetic algorithms and the cross-entropy method, with supporting citations. MAPPO also gains a reference. The established positioning relative to discrete diffusion, PMD and online reinforcement learning is retained.

P1.justification: The main section sequence and much foundational prose are retained. v3 copyedits wording, repairs the malformed Zekri citation, clarifies that 'on-policy' refers to diffusion trajectories, adds a practitioner-guidance subsection and explanatory appendices, and updates author and affiliation text.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout with running headers. v3 adds a framework flowchart and several analysis figures, merges v1 Figures 3 and 4 into Figure 5, expands comparison tables, and relocates Table 5 to the end. Existing plots are extensively resized, rearranged or redrawn, with improved labels and captions.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's limited Football comparison and weak guidance on choosing FKL versus RKL through stronger baselines, expanded uncertainty reporting, controlled comparisons and explicit failure analyses. Mathematical corrections also improve technical clarity. These gains are tempered by conflicting new Atari aggregates: Figure 8 reports RL-D2 mean/IQM 34.7/5.5, while Table 6 reports 31.33/4.98. Despite that reporting flaw, the comparative validation and practical understanding improve substantially; higher Football scores under larger budgets are not themselves evidence of improvement.
